newsitem.title: UK: LucasVarity sees higher post-merger savings.
newsitem.headline: LucasVarity sees higher post-merger savings.

text.p: Anglo-U.S. auto components group LucasVarity Plc said it expected to boost operating profits substantially more than it previously thought, following a 3-month review into how to reshape the group, after the merger of Lucas Industries and Varity Corp.

"In the three months since the merger was consummated, intensive studies by transition teams have identified annual operating savings of 120 million stg, to be achieved by January 31, 1999," the company said in a statement. "This level of savings is significantly greater than the 65 million stg anticipated at the time the merger was announced last May."
Also, as previously flagged, it should realise at least 65 million stg in tax savings over the next two years.

To achieve the savings across its core operations will involve reducing the group's worldwide number of employees by 3,000 over the next two years. It will be covered by a one-off exceptional charge of about 120 million stg.

"An additional, one-time, largely non-cash exceptional charge of approximately 130 million stg will be recognised, primarily representing asset writedowns. The total of these one-time charges, 250 million stg, will be recorded in the period ending January 31, 1997," LucasVarity said.

Commenting on the rationalisation moves, chief executive Victor Rice, who came from the Varity side of the merger, said "the combination fo cost savings and anticipated revenue growth identified by these teams will help the company achieve the aggressive performance targets it has set for itself."
LucasVarity is involved in the design, manufacture and supply of systems, products and services in international automotive, diesel engine, after-market and aerospace industries.
Both parties in the merger specialised in braking systems and industry sources expected that many of the rationalisation measures would affect production and employment in these units.
